segments: 1 Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
they sated him with (inflicted on him) disgrace,
and brought him before the fortress of Qati'a, in which his wife was placed.
And when the Turks commanded him to tell his wife to surrender the fortress,
he, still in his madness, was deceiving the Turks,
and said to his wife:
"Surrender the fortress.
And this is a sign for you:
that some days ago I sent to you a youth named Midas,"
meaning "do not give [it up]" in Armenian.
And when the Turks found out,
they killed him
and cast him to the dogs.
And Ibn Danishmand brought Bohemond, the Frankish king, to Melitene
and sold him for one hundred thousand dinars.
And that Bohemond gave Antioch to his sister's son,
and he himself returned to his own country.
And in the year
(1414 of the Greeks [1102/3 AD]:
he was [there],
and the Arabs heard
that there was [only] a small number with him,
the armies of the Turks that were in Tripoli, Damascus, and Hims gathered against him.
And that Frankish king, because there were only three hundred horsemen with him,
sent out one hundred against the Damascenes,
one hundred against those of Tripoli,
and fifty against the people of Hims,
and chose fifty to be with him.
And when they met one another,
the people of Hims and the Damascenes quickly fled toward the mountains;
and they were more than five thousand.
The forces of Tripoli, however, who were about three thousand,
persevered in the fight.
And when Saint-Gilles saw that the Franks (the Turks? {OCR?}) were prevailing,
he came against them in person with the fifty Franks who were with him,
and routed them.
And he also pursued after those fugitives,
and they killed about seven thousand of the Arabs.
And he departed from Cilicia,
and came and encamped against Tripoli,
and waged fierce war against it.
And he captured Antartus (Tortosa),
and killed all the Arabs who were in it,
and he also attacked other fortresses.
And another count also came by sea and besieged Acre,
and hard pressed it.
And they also took control over Edessa,
and began taking captive and devastating the regions of Syria that were in the hands of the Arabs and Turks.
And in the year 498 [AH],
notes: [Note:] 110[3] of our Lord?: when Saint-Gilles [was] in the city of Tarsus
[Note:] 498 of the Arabs: when they prevailed over Sultan Rukn al-Din Berkyaruq
